1.0 INTRODUCTION
1.1 Purpose
This document defines the specific requirements to be satisfied throughout the implement ation of the software for
the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME) instrument. The information contained within this document
provides the technical requirements to be implemented and enables the development team to assess whether or not
the completed software complies with the requirements of the system. The data included in this document provides
the criteria for acceptance of the integrated software configuration.
1.2 Scope
The requirements specified herein apply only to SAME instrument software and custom MSG Laptop Computer
(MLC) software. All ground based telemetry data processing and command uplink software requirements will be
identified in future documents as required.
1.3 Applicable Documents

Experiment, Rev. 1.01, Dr. David Urban, NASA Glenn Research Center,
January 3, 2005.

SAME-DOC-004 Rev D
2
2.0 INSTRUMENT OVERVIEW
The SAME instrument is designed to quantify the size and distribution of smoke particulate in low gravity so that
this information is available for the future design of effective low gravity smoke det ectors. The instrument will also
be used to evaluate the performance of two existing U.S. spacecraft smoke detectors and one commercial smoke
detector. Measurements will be made for the smoke from several materials found in spacecraft considering the
effects of sample temperature, air flow, smoke residence time and aging. The primary targets are materials that
produce liquid smoke particulate but solid smoke producers will also be considered.

Figure 1 SAME Instrument Assembly Inside MSG WV
The instrument is installed and operated in the MSG Work Volume (WV) which provides a minimal level of
containment (see Figure 1). A general description of the major subsystems follows below. See SAME-DOC-001,
Concept Description Document, for more detail.
• Sample Carousel Turning Module, Sample Carousel and Heater Wire Coil
These components are used to select and heat a sample in order to generate smoke.
• Camera
A camera and light(s) are mounted to see the sample and production of smoke.
• Aging Chamber
The aging chamber has a piston and two gate valves for holding the smoke for a time before releasing it
downstream. The piston is moved by pressure and vacuum provided by MSG and controlled by SAME.
• Thermal Precipitator Module
This assembly collects samples of smoke on TEM grids for post-flight inspection. It has access to smoke
before and after the aging chamber.

filename: PSI-101_Reference Data_SAME_Software Requirement Document_004 Rev D.pdf
source_path: same-r/PSI-101_Reference Data_SAME_Software Requirement Document_004 Rev D.pdf
text:
SAME-DOC-004 Rev D
3
• Smoke Diagnostics
After the aging chamber, the smoke is passed to several diagnostics: the TSI P-Trak™ particle
concentration counter, the TSI DustTrak™, a residential-grade ionization detector, the ISS photoelectric
smoke detector and the STS ionization smoke detector.
• Fluids Control Unit
Pressure and vacuum supplied by MSG is controlled for smoke aging chamber piston movement and for all
other fluid flow to and from the diagnostic equipment.
• System Diagnostics
Besides the diagnostic instruments measuring smoke characteristics, there are pressure transducers,
temperature gauges, and voltage and current sensors to monitor system performance.
• External Interfaces
External interfaces provided by MSG include power, video recording, temperature control, post -
pyrolization venting, nitrogen and air supply/vacuum, an RS-422 interface for commanding and telemetry,
ethernet for file transfer, and a laptop for crew access to the SAME experiment. A SAMS unit measures
local µg and vibrations and forwards that data to the ground requiring no SAME or MSG processing.
• Avionics
Contained in the Data Acquisition Control Unit (DACU) box, the SAME avionics conduct automated
experiments, controlling the other sub-systems to produce and analyze the smoke. Commands from the
ground are processed. Experiment data is saved to files on a local storage medium and forwarded to MSG
for subsequent downlink. Housekeeping data is downlinked every second and supplied to MSG. Off -
nominal conditions are reported to MSG and the ground. In addition, a means for the crew to access
SAME data and control is provided.

source_path: same-r/PSI-101_Reference Data_SAME_Software Requirement Document_004 Rev D.pdf
text:
SAME-DOC-004 Rev D
4
3.0 AVIONICS OVERVIEW
SAME avionics are located in the DACU within the MSG Work Volume (WV). Cables will stretch to the SAME
diagnostic hardware for control and feedback, to J311 of the WV for command and data transfer, and to J404 of the
WV for ethernet connection to the MSG laptop computer (MLC) for file transfer and crew display operation. There
is also a cable for the camera.
3.1 Data Interfaces
To interface to the MSG, and subsequently to ground systems, the DACU CPU will communicate primarily to the
MSG Rack Controller, also known as the SPLC (Standard Payload Computer) using an RS-422 interface (see Figure
2). SAME will use this interface to receive uplink commands and send health and status (H&S) data and low rate
telemetry (LRT) data.

Figure 2 SAME to MSG Data Interfaces
Payload commands are transmitted from the ground through the ISS Payload MDM and eventually to the SPLC via
MIL-STD-1553. The SPLC abstracts this interface from the payload developer, relieving the burden of knowing the
details about the 1553 bus and command validation.
A packet containing SAME health and status is automatically transmitted in the reverse direction on the 1553 bus
and is received on the ground. Also included in the payload health and status packet is the Experiment Control
Word or ECW, a single dedicated memory word that represents the status of the payload. The ECW is monitored by
various ISS subsystems and provides a quick alert if an off-nominal condition is indicated in it.

filename: PSI-101_Reference Data_SAME_Software Requirement Document_004 Rev D.pdf
source_path: same-r/PSI-101_Reference Data_SAME_Software Requirement Document_004 Rev D.pdf
text:
SAME-DOC-004 Rev D
5
File-based SAME science data such as experiment measurement data and instrument ancillary data will be
transferred to the MLC using FTP utilizing a 10BaseT ethernet connection. Once these files are stored on the MLC,
the MSG Operations Team at the Payload Operations Integration Center (POIC) will periodically initiate their
downlink and forward them to the SAME Operations Team. Since SAME is not permitted to transmit data on the
ISS LAN, the DACU will automatically switch the active network connection fro m the MLC to SAME and ISS
using a custom designed ethernet switch when the FTP transfer is required. In its normal state, the MLC will be
connected to ISS LAN.
The camera looking at the SAME sample is hooked up via an NTSC cable to a feedthrough inside the WV which is
then patched on the outside to a video recorder channel in the video drawer.
3.2 DACU Overview
The DACU is the central point for SAME control. It is ultimately responsible for all experiment operations and
interfacing with the environment external to SAME. It contains all of the logic necessary to autonomously operate
experiments. A brief list of its major responsibilities is as follows:
1. Receive, validate and process commands from the MSG.
2. Periodically transmit SAME system status and select parameters to the MSG.
3. Transmit completed and requested data files to the MLC via FTP.
4. Manage and store all science and system files on the local data storage medium.
5. Autonomously control the progress of preprogrammed tests.
6. Provide diagnostic information and manual control of all sensors and controls using the GSE port.
7. Control the MSG video recorder(s) capturing SAME images.
8. React to sensor(s) out of tolerance by notifying MSG and ground systems, and performing software inhibits
or other actions as appropriate.
3.3 Crew Display Overview
During long periods of LOS or failure of telemetry, it is beneficial to provide limited visibility into SAME
operation. Payloads may utilize the MLC to present payload status to the crew and provide a mechanism to control
the payload directly from it. Two options for providing the SAME Crew Display are possible. Option 1 is the
preferred solution at this time because of a likely delay in an upgrade to provide a dedicated ethernet link between
the MLC and an experiment.
3.3.1 Option 1 - Custom Win32 or Java Based Application
All data transmitted to the SPLC via H&S and LRT is also transmitted to the MLC via the MSG 1553 bus, and is
therefore available on the MLC. SAME may develop a custom Win32-based or Java-based application that displays
a limited set of the SAME downlink data for the crew to see and provides commanding to the SAME instrument.
3.3.2 Option 2 - Embedded Web Pages
A dedicated ethernet interface between the MLC and SAME may be leveraged to provide a web-based interface into
the DACU using the MLC native web browser. The operating system running on the DACU is capable of running
an embedded web-server such as Apache or NASA’s Tempest servers.

text:
SAME-DOC-004 Rev D
6
4.0 SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS
4.1 System Status
4.1.1 Update Rate
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-1-1-1-1] The DACU software shall update its internal status once per second.
4.1.2 LED Status Indicators
The DACU will control two LEDs mounted on the outside of the DACU enclosure using discrete outputs. These
LEDs are described in Table 1.

Table 1 Status LEDs
LED Name Description
OK STATUS Indicates nominal operation of the entire
SAME apparatus.
TEST RUNNING Indicates that a test is currently running.

[SAME-SW-REQ-4-1-2-1-1] The DACU shall illuminate the OK STATUS LED while the CPU is
properly running. If the software detects an internal fault or error condition,
the LED shall be extinguished.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-1-2-1-2] The DACU shall illuminate the TEST RUNNING LED while a test is
running. Upon completion, the LED shall be extinguished.
4.2 Data Communication
There are three two-way paths of data communications connected to the DACU. An RS422 interface is used for
communications with the SPLC. An ethernet interface is used for communications with MLC. An RS232 interface
is available while not on orbit for development, maintenance, and debugging activities.
4.2.1 SPLC Communications
4.2.1.1 Serial Port Configuration
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-1-1] A single bi-directional RS422 channel between the DACU and the SPLC
shall be used to communicate with the MSG systems.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-1-2] RS422 serial port settings shall be 19200 baud, no parity, 8 data bits, and 1
stop bit.

SAME-DOC-004 Rev D
7
4.2.1.2 Data Format
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-2-1] All data that the DACU transmits to and accepts from the SPLC shall
conform to the ESTEC Data Link Format as specified in MSG-ORIGIN-IC-
0001, MSG RC ASW Interface Control Document, section 3.5.1.1.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-2-2] All data that the DACU transmits to and accepts from the SPLC shall
conform to the byte and bit order as specified in MSG-ORIGIN-IC-0001,
MSG RC ASW Interface Control Document, section 1.4.3.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-2-3] All data that the DACU transmits to and accepts from the SPLC shall
conform to the word alignment as specified in MSG-ORIGIN-IC-0001,
MSG RC ASW Interface Control Document, section 2.3.
4.2.1.3 Health and Status Packet
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-3-1] Once per second, the DACU shall transmit to the SPLC a health and status
packet containing information such as voltages, currents, and pressures
necessary to verify safe and proper operation. Included in this information
are the C&W flags which indicate nominal or off-nominal operation to the
rack systems.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-3-2] The content of the health and status packet shall conform to the format
specified in MSG-ORIGIN-IC-0001, MSG RC ASW Interface Control
Document.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-3-3] The Cycle Counter field in the health and status packet shall be incremented
once per second up to the value 0xffff, then roll over to 0.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-3-4] The C&W flags fields in the health and status packet shall be asserted only
upon the conditions listed in Section 6.2.
4.2.1.4 Low Rate Telemetry Packet
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-4-1] Once per second, the DACU shall transmit to the SPLC a low rate telemetry
packet representing the current state of the instrument.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-4-2] The content of the low rate telemetry packet shall conform to the format
specified in MSG-ORIGIN-IC-0001, MSG RC ASW Interface Control
Document.
4.2.1.5 Video Command Packet
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-5-1] The DACU shall have the ability to control MSG video drawer functions by
sending video command packets to the SPLC. The controllable video
drawer functions are determined by the requirements of the video drawer
command group, Section 4.4.5.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-5-2] The content of video drawer packets issued by the DACU shall conform to
the format specified in MSG-ORIGIN-IC-0001, MSG RC ASW Interface
Control Document.
4.2.1.6 Time of Day Packet
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-6-1] The DACU shall accept time of day packets from the SPLC when they
adhere to the format specified in MSG-ORIGIN-IC-0001, MSG RC ASW
Interface Control Document.

source_path: same-r/PSI-101_Reference Data_SAME_Software Requirement Document_004 Rev D.pdf
text:
SAME-DOC-004 Rev D
8
4.2.1.7 Experiment Command Packet
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-1-7-1] The DACU shall accept experiment command packets from the SPLC when
they adhere to the format specified in MSG-ORIGIN-IC-0001, MSG RC
ASW Interface Control Document.
4.2.2 MLC Communications
Upon completion of a science run, all data files will be stored on DACU internal storage. A copy of these data files
will automatically be forwarded to the MLC via FTP on a point-to-point cross-wired ethernet cable. The SAME
Operations Team will submit a request to the MSG Team at MSFC to downlink the files on the M LC at the earliest
possible time. The downlinked files will then be electronically forwarded to GRC. Because the connection is made
directly to the MLC, no bandwidth restrictions are necessary to ensure ISS LAN resource availability.
4.2.2.1 FTP Usage
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-2-1-1] All data files stored on the DACU local storage shall be automatically
forwarded to the MLC via FTP for backup and downlink.
4.2.2.2 Network Details
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-2-2-1] A dedicated standard 802.3 (10BaseT) ethernet connection from the MLC
to the DACU shall be used to perform the FTP transfer.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-2-2-2] Communications with the FTP server shall be done utilizing a server IP
address of 192.168.1.1, port 21.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-2-2-3] The DACU will automatically switch the ethernet source from MLC→ISS
to MLC→SAME when communication to the MLC is required. When the
transaction is completed, the original MLC→ISS connection will be
restored.
4.2.2.3 SAME File Maintenance
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-2-3-1] The DACU shall provide the ability to remove SAME files from the FTP
server as needed to ensure proper storage space utilization.
4.2.3 Remote Console Communications
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-3-1-1] The DACU shall provide a telnet console login session on an RS232 port.
All administrative features and capabilities available via telnet shall be
supported.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-2-3-1-2] The telnet console RS232 serial port settings shall be, 19200 baud, no
parity, 8 data bits, and 1 stop bit.

text:
SAME-DOC-004 Rev D
9
4.3 Data Storage Requirements
The data storage requirements reflect two main needs. First, that a record of all status, measurements and events is
preserved beyond the flight of the instrument. And second, that individual values of status, measurements or events
can be easily located in stored data.
4.3.1 Storage Media
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-3-1-1-1] The DACU shall store all files on a media that can preserve all generated
files for extraction after payload down-mass.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-3-1-1-2] The storage media shall have a capacity of at least 520 megabytes.
4.3.2 File Conventions
4.3.2.1 Directory Structure
Because the execution of ISS instrument experiments are highly scheduled, the date and time that procedures and
ground commanding is performed is usually reliably recorded by NASA cadre and experiment ground operation
teams. As such, finding the data files for a previously run experiment or for a particular logged event is facilitated
by a data storage structure based on the date. Therefore,
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-3-2-1-1] All files created shall be organized into a hierarchical directory structure
based on the date that files were created.
4.3.2.2 File Names
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-3-2-2-1] All files created shall have unique file names.
4.3.3 Stored Data
4.3.3.1 Housekeeping Data
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-3-3-1-1] Once per second data relating to the status of the instrument shall be stored
to a file.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-3-3-1-2] Each second of housekeeping data stored to a file shall be time-tagged.
4.3.3.2 Messages
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-3-3-2-1] Messages generated by the instrument shall be stored to a file.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-3-3-2-2] Each message stored to a file shall be time-tagged.
4.3.3.3 Experiment Results
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-3-3-3-1] Experiment results shall be stored to a file
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-3-3-3-2] Experiment results stored to a file shall be time-tagged.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-3-3-3-3] DELETED.

4.4 Command Requirements
Commands are the primary means of initiating SAME instrument operations. Commands to an instrument are
typically formatted into an array of data and inserted into command packets and then transmitted from the ground
operation station or from the crew display on the MSG MLC on-board the ISS. When command packets reach the
DACU the command data within is extracted and interpreted and the appropriate software functions are executed.
The command requirements below deal mainly with the functions required by the instrument and not with how those
functions are implemented or with how the command data is formatte d. See SAME-DOC-005, Software Interface
Control Document, for the latter information.
4.4.1 General Command Requirements
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-4-1-1-1] DELETED
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-4-1-1-2] DELETED

Table 2 DELETED
DELETED

[SAME-SW-REQ-4-4-1-1-3] At the start of execution of a command the DACU shall generate and
downlink a message that includes the name of the command and its
parameters.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-4-1-1-4] At the successful completion of a command the DACU shall generate and
downlink a message announcing the successful completion.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-4-1-1-5] The DACU shall perform out-of-bound checking on all command
parameters and reject commands with out-of-bound parameters.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-4-1-1-6] The bounds for command parameters shall be those specified in SAME-
DOC-005, Software Interface Control Document.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-4-1-1-7] The DACU shall allow for suspension of bound checking on command
parameters.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-4-1-1-8] The DACU shall indicate when a command is being executed with bound
checking suspended.
4.4.2 System Command Group
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-4-2-1-1] The DACU shall accept a set of commands to perform system level
operations. The system group commands shall perform the operations listed
in Table 3.

Table 3 System Command Group
Command Name Operation Description
NoOp Command generates the required received and complete messages but
performs no operation. Useful for a quick test of the command inter face.
Initialize Initialize hardware components and prepares the system to run a test.
Shutdown Perform an orderly system shutdown.
Reset Reset the computer running the software.
SelfTest Perform a system self-test and report the result.
OSCommand Execute an operating system level command as if it were entered at the
command prompt.
FTPCommand Perform an FTP command
SetDigitalOutput Turn on or off the specified digital output.
SetAnalogOutput Set the output of the specified analog output channel.
ClearEvents Clears all outstanding events
IgnoreBounds Bounds checking is suspended for only the next command sent after this
one.
SetRegistryValue Manually sets a value in the file registry.

4.4.3 Test Command Group
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-4-3-1-1] The DACU shall accept a set of commands to perform automated tests. The
test group commands shall perform the operations listed in Table 4.

Table 4 Test Command Group
Command Name Operation Description

if it has any undefined or invalid parameters then an error shall be
generated and the test shall be aborted.
PauseTest Suspend the currently running test
ResumeTest Resume a currently running test that has been suspended.
AbortTest Stop the currently running test, otherwise it finishes on its own.

4.4.4 Test Configuration Command Group
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-4-4-1-1] The DACU shall accept a set of commands to configure test parameters.
The test configuration group commands shall perform the operations listed
in Table 5. All operations are for a specified test.

source_path: same-r/PSI-101_Reference Data_SAME_Software Requirement Document_004 Rev D.pdf
text:
SAME-DOC-004 Rev D
12
Table 5 Test Configuration Command Group
Command Name Operation Description
SetSampleNumber Sets the desired sample number for the test.
SetCarouselNumber Set the carousel number (for reference only, not for control of which
carousel is installed).
SetInletVelocity Sets the target flow velocity for the inlet duct during sample heating.
SetHeaterSetpoint Sets the resistance/temperature setpoint of the heater controller.
SetHeaterDuration Sets the duration of the sample heating sequence.
SetHeaterPIDCoefficients Sets the PID control coefficients for the heater sequence.
SetMixingDuration Sets the time that the mixing fan is on.
SetThermalPrecipitatorChannel Sets which channels the smoke will be sent to on the thermal
precipitator unit for pre-aged and post-aged smoke.
SetPrimaryAgingDuration Sets the duration that smoke is kept in the smoke aging chamber.
SetSecondaryAgingDuration Sets an optional extended aging duration that applies to a portion of
the total smoke.
SetSecondaryAgingVolume Sets the portion of smoke left in the smoke aging chamber for the
optional secondary aging duration.
SetLFEFlowRate Sets the dilution rate for the P-Trak in terms of the laminar flow
element (LFE) flow rate. This is the target amount of smoke aerosol
reaching the P-Trak. Dilution GN2 makes up the remainder of the
700 sccm flowing to the P-Trak.
SetTestSetup Sets a number of discretes indicating which diagnostics should be
used and other test setup variables.
DownlinkTestParameters Downlinks all parameters of a specified test.
CreateNewTest Creates a new test with the specified number and configures it with
default values. Error occurs if test already exists.

4.5 Experiment Sequencing Requirements
4.5.1 Miscellaneous Sequencing Requirements
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-5-1-1-1] Residence time of smoke in the aging chamber shall be controllable from 0
to 100 (or greater) minutes per aging period.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-5-1-1-2] The DACU shall command the diagnostic instruments to sample the smoke
once the diagnostic duct is filled from the aging chamber.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-5-1-1-3] The DACU shall control the timing of diagnostic measurements such that a
steady state signal is achieved on all instruments.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-5-1-1-4] The DACU shall allow the option of multiple smoke samples from the
aging chamber with separate aging times.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-5-1-1-5] The DACU shall purge the diagnostic duct between multiple smoke
samples from the aging chamber.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-5-1-1-6] The DACU shall control the system to allow the P-Trak to sample air from
the MSG work volume.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-5-1-1-7] The DACU shall control the system to allow the DustTrak to sample air
from the MSG work volume.

[SAME-SW-REQ-4-5-2-1-1] DELETED.

Principal Investigator.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-5-3-1-3] Additional tests shall be possible to define with parameters determined by
uplink commands.
[SAME-SW-REQ-4-5-3-1-4] It shall be possible to confirm all parameters for a specific test.

5.0 SUBSYSTEM REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Sample Carousel
5.1.1 Sample Selection
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-1-1-1-1] The DACU shall control a motor to rotate the sample carousel to a specified
sample number.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-1-1-1-2] The DACU shall use four proximity sensors to confirm correct positioning
of the correct sample carousel.
5.1.2 Sample Positioning
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-1-2-1-1] The DACU shall mate the selected sample tube with the smoke generation
duct and the sample contacts with heater wire coil contacts by controlling a
linear actuator.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-1-2-1-2] The DACU shall confirm correct mating of a sample tube and sample
contacts by monitoring the resistance between the two heater wire coil
contacts.
5.2 Sample Heater (Heater Wire Coil)
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-2-1-1-1] The DACU in combination with the heater microcontroller shall control the
sample surface temperature and duration of the heating.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-2-1-1-2] The DACU in combination with the heater microcontroller shall achieve
steady state temperature of the heater within 5 seconds.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-2-1-1-3] The DACU in combination with the heater microcontroller shall set the
temperature of the heater wire coil to any temperature between 50 and 500
degrees Celcius.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-2-1-1-4] The DACU in combination with the heater microcontroller shall provide
active temperature control of the heater.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-2-1-1-5] The DACU in combination with the heater microcontroller shall control the
heater temperature and duration so as not to ignite the sample.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-2-1-1-6] The DACU shall measure and store the sample temperature at least once per
second.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-2-1-1-7] The DACU shall measure and store the gas plume temperature at least once
per second.
5.3 Camera and Lighting
5.3.1 Lighting
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-3-1-1-1] The DACU shall control power to any combination of the camera lights.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-3-1-1-2] DELETED.

5.3.2 Camera
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-3-2-1-1] The DACU shall control the gain and gamma settings of the camera.
5.4 Aging Chamber
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-4-1-1-1] The DACU shall control the aging chamber piston upward velocity to
achieve 1 to 10 cm/s average flow velocity in the smoke generation duct.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-4-1-1-2] The DACU shall control the aging chamber piston upward movement by
controlling a solenoid on the vacuum line, by sensing and controlling a
mass flow controller on the vacuum line, and by sensing a pressure
transducer monitoring the drive side pressure of the piston.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-4-1-1-3] The DACU shall control the aging chamber piston downward velocity in
order to provide smoke at the rate required for the particular diagnostics in
use.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-4-1-1-4] The DACU shall control the aging chamber piston downward movement by
controlling a solenoid on the GN2 line, by sensing and controlling a mass
flow controller on the GN2 line, and by sensing a pressure transducer
monitoring the sample side pressure of the piston.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-4-1-1-5] The DACU shall control a mixing fan in the aging chamber to be on during
a specified portion of the residence time.
5.5 Thermal Precipitator Module
5.5.1 Valve Control
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-5-1-1-1] Using digital outputs the DACU shall control the valves of the thermal
precipitator module so that at most only one valve is open at a time.
5.5.2 Heater Control
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-5-2-1-1] Using a digital output the DACU shall control power to one thermal
precipitator module heater at a time.
5.6 DustTrak
5.6.1 Control
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-6-1-1-1] The DACU shall control the DustTrak via an RS-232 serial port.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-6-1-1-2] The DACU shall turn the DustTrak on and off by controlling the on/off
keypad using custom electronics.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-6-1-1-3] The DACU shall control the DustTrak keypad using custom electronics.
5.6.2 Data Reception
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-6-2-1-1] The DACU shall receive data from the DustTrak via an RS-232 serial port.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-6-2-1-2] The DACU shall sample DustTrak data at a minimum rate of 0.2 Hz.

The ISS detector is an Allied Signal/HoneywellTM engineering model.

The STS detector is a Brunswick DefenseTM engineering model.
[SAME-SW-REQ-5-10-1-1-1] The DACU shall control the STS detector.

[SAME-SW-REQ-5-11-1-1-1] The DACU shall control the dilution of smoke using analog input(s) and

6.0 OFF-NOMINAL AND CONTINGENCY REQUIREMENTS
6.1 Maintenance Mode Operation
The software will contain provisions to allow experiment operations to continue in the event of the following:
[SAME-SW-REQ-6-1-1-1-1] In the event of a loss of the ability to write to the data hard drive, the system
shall continue to accept uplink commands and transmit status data to ensure
safe operation.
[SAME-SW-REQ-6-1-1-1-2] In the event of a loss of ethernet communication between the DACU and
the MLC, operations shall continue. Data recorded on the flight avionics
may be manually commanded for retransmission once communication is
regained.
6.2 Caution and Warning
Three discrete bits in the health and status packet are used to indicate to MSG the presence of a payload condition
warranting a warning, caution, or advisory classification and reaction. See MSFC -RQMT-2888, MSG Investigation
Interface Requirements Document, Section 3.11 for details of each level. The specific payload conditions that result
in warning and caution levels are determined by the Payload Safety Review Panel (PSRP) during Phased Safety
Reviews. Automatic safing will be performed if the warning or caution bit is set. The advisory bit can be used to
reflect errors and off-nominal conditions seen only in the low rate telemetry data to the health and status data. If,
due to limited communication coverage or communication error, the health and status data is received while the low
rate telemetry is not, then these off-nominal conditions will still be noted and time-tagged.
6.2.1 Warning
There are no conditions that constitute a “Class 2 -Warning” condition and a subsequent set of the Warning bit in the
Health and Status packet payload ECW.
6.2.2 Caution
There are no conditions that constitute a “Class 3 - Caution” condition and a subsequent set of the Caution bit in the
Health and Status packet payload ECW.
6.2.3 Advisory
There are no conditions that constitute a “Class 4 - Advisory” condition and a subsequent set of the Advisory bit in
the Health and Status packet payload ECW.
6.3 Automatic Safing
[SAME-SW-REQ-6-3-1-1-1] In the event of a GN2 regulated pressure reading of over 21 psig, the DACU
shall automatically shut off the main GN2 valve.
[SAME-SW-REQ-6-3-1-1-2] In the event of a vacuum pressure reading of over 19 psia, the DACU shall
automatically shut off the main vacuum valve.

7.0 CREW DISPLAY REQUIREMENTS
7.1 Graphic Standards
The development and approval process for the project crew display follows the guidelines in SSP 58700-ANX5,
U.S. Payload Operations Data File Management Plan, Annex 5: Payload Display Review , and in SSP 58700-
ANX6, U.S. Payload Operations Data File Management Plan, Annex 6: Payload Developers Review Guide .
[SAME-SW-REQ-7-1-1-1-1] The crew display shall meet all applicable standards defined in SSP 50313,
Display and Graphics Commonality Standard.
7.2 Interfaces
7.2.1 Host Computer
[SAME-SW-REQ-7-2-1-1-1] The crew display shall be able to run on the MSG Laptop Computer with
features and operating system as described in MSFC-RQMT-2888,
Microgravity Science Glovebox Investigation Interface Requirements
Document, Section 3.3.5.
7.2.2 MLC Server

[SAME-SW-REQ-7-2-2-1-1] The crew display shall send commands from the MLC to the instrument
using the MLC Server Socket Interface.
[SAME-SW-REQ-7-2-2-1-2] The crew display on the MLC shall receive health and status data and low-
rate telemetry from the instrument using the MLC Server Socket Interface.
[SAME-SW-REQ-7-2-2-1-3] The crew display shall meet the MLC Server Socket Interface requirements
documented in MSFC-RQMT-3098, Software Requirements Specification
(SRS) for Microgravity Science Glovebox Laptop Computer Server
Software, Section 4.6.
7.3 Features
7.3.1 Commanding
[SAME-SW-REQ-7-3-1-1-1] The crew display shall include a subset of the full instrument command list.
7.3.2 Data Display
[SAME-SW-REQ-7-3-2-1-1] The crew display shall display a subset of the full instrument health and
status and/or low-rate telemetry data.

The software necessary for developmental purposes is subject to change; therefore the items in this section are not

will maintain a true list of necessary software for development tasks.

[SAME-SW-REQ-8-1-1-1-2] Software will be provided to support test structures and instrumentation to

[SAME-SW-REQ-8-1-1-1-3] DELETED.

[SAME-SW-REQ-8-1-1-1-5] Software will be provided to support test structures and instrumentation to

[SAME-SW-REQ-8-1-1-1-6] Software will be provided to test and characterize the accuracy of the heater
temperature.
[SAME-SW-REQ-8-1-1-1-7] Software will be provided to support a test rig for characterization of mass
